fields.v: Construction: engineers author requirement chains, reference deltas, tests and Docker environments (LLM-assisted drafting) -> two independent reviewers check coherence and instruction-test-solution alignment -> oracle verification -> cross-validation (traceability, shortcut audit). Evaluation per task: one container and session; each round deliver instruction -> agent edits -> cumulative verifier -> next round only on pass (fail-stop); 4 attempts. SR: fast-forward to reference state, then solve target round

fields.v: Tasks: 26 multi-round tasks. Configurations: 13 models on the same Terminus-2 harness, Harbor protocol, environment, tool interface and standard prompt (no model-specific prompt engineering). Baseline/control: SR condition (reference fast-forward) contrasted with persistent MT@4. Acceptance: cumulative executable behavioural tests verified on the reference solution. Repetitions: 4 independent attempts per agent-task in multi-round; SR single attempt. Human intervention: none; simulated user rounds, fail-stop after first failing round. Not held constant: model reasoning settings (Table 6: high reasoning effort for Opus-4.7, GPT-5.5, DeepSeek-V4-Pro/Flash, MiMo-V2.5-Pro, Gemini-3.1-Pro, Doubao-Seed-2.0-Pro; thinking enabled for GLM-5.1, Kimi-K2.6, Qwen3.6-Plus, Qwen3.5-397B; default for Opus-4.6; reasoning split for MiniMax-M2.7)

fields.v: Opus-4.7 best (54.0 MT@4, 42.3% completion), GPT-5.5 52.4; only these two exceed half of the multi-round credit. SR exceeds MT@4 by 21.9-39.5 points for all agents except MiMo-V2.5-Pro; Opus-4.6 has the highest SR (78.9) but ranks third on MT@4 (44.0). Top/lower tier ratio 5.9x under MT@4 vs 2.3x under SR. Round pass rate falls from 46.7 (round 1) to 21.3 (round 5) and 7.7 (round 10); 57.0% of failed MT rounds are solvable under SR. Document-driven tasks (AGENTS.md or spec files) average 50.1 MT@4, about 2.4x explorative (20.9) and contractual (20.7) tasks; authors: may reflect a persistent readable reference, sample (4 tasks, 31 rounds) too small for causal claims. Review-driven activity highest (29.6), specification evolution lowest (21.8). Failing trials use 1.1-3.1x more output tokens than passing ones at the same round. No significance tests

fields.v: Yes per the authors: MT@4 separates tiers more sharply than SR and reranks agents; MT@4 and SR together separate accumulated-state damage from round difficulty. Cross-attempt consistency falls with depth (reliability ratio 67% at round 1, 20% at round 5). Limitations stated: fail-stop does not measure recovery; small task count; taxonomy cells small, so category patterns are diagnostic rather than stable rankings; expensive (24.4B tokens)

fields.v: Only 26 tasks, limited by manual authoring, cumulative tests, cross-validation and evaluation cost. Fail-stop may underestimate agents able to recover (SR partly addresses this). Only tasks verifiable by executable tests; subjective design decisions, code quality and collaborative negotiation not evaluated. Restart strategies not evaluated. Gaps / future work: adaptive multi-turn evaluation with an examiner agent; separate recovery protocol; system support such as regression checks between rounds, repository-grounded summaries of active requirements and workspace audits; larger document-driven sample
